facts.statement: Fossils of Potamornis were found in the Lance Formation at Buck Creek in the USA.
facts.quote: Its scrappy remains were found in the Lance Formation at Buck Creek, USA

facts.statement: Possible remains of Potamornis were found in the upper Hell Creek Formation of Montana, though these may have been reworked from the Danian age of the Paleogene period.
facts.quote: additional possible remains were found in the upper Hell Creek Formation of Montana, dated to the Danian age of the Paleogene period, though these may have been reworked

facts.statement: The only known species, Potamornis skutchi, was named and described in 2001.
facts.quote: A single species was named and described in 2001: Potamornis skutchi

facts.statement: Potamornis is almost certainly a member of the Hesperornithes, a group of hefty, toothed, flightless diving birds from the Mesozoic seas.
facts.quote: This was almost certainly a member of the Hesperornithes, the hefty and toothed flightless diving birds of the Mesozoic seas

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis suggests Potamornis shares more unique traits with the family Hesperornithidae than other aspects of its anatomy might imply.
facts.quote: the quadrate bone is unique in some respects but apparently shares more apomorphies with the family Hesperornithidae - the "typical" Hesperornithes - in cladistic analysis

facts.statement: Potamornis was heavily built like other diving birds and weighed approximately 1.5 to 2 kilograms.
facts.quote: Though it was heavily built like many (flying and flightless) diving birds, it weighed perhaps 1.5 or 2 kg

facts.statement: Potamornis is classified within the subclass Hesperornithes.
The genus Potamornis was established by Elzanowski, Paul & Stidham in 2001.
Potamornis lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that flightlessness within the Hesperornithes may have evolved independently in different lineages, including Potamornis.
facts.quote: This raises the possibility that the Hesperornithes not only included flying members (see also Enaliornis), but that their families might have evolved flightlessness independently

rejected.statement: Potamornis lived during the late Maastrichtian age of the late Cretaceous period.
rejected.quote: Potamornis is a prehistoric bird genus that dated back to the late Maastrichtian age of the late Cretaceous period
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'late Maastrichtian age of the late Cretaceous period'
